MacPaw announces a long-term strategic partnership with Liquid AI to jointly develop an on-device AI technology stack designed specifically for Mac.

The collaboration will begin with Eney, MacPaw's macOS AI assistant.

MacPaw partners with Liquid AI to bring more on-device AI capabilities to Mac.

Liquid AI's Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) will be adapted for accessibility features on the Mac platform, and combined with MacPaw's proprietary on-device technologies: Mnemos, which handles memory functions, and Elix, which handles inference functions.

Eney switched to local models last year, keeping reasoning, contextual search, skill execution and conversation history processed on-device wherever possible.

This new partnership aims to further deepen that approach. The two companies will jointly develop the underlying technology stack, rather than MacPaw simply plugging in another third-party model.

MacPaw said that once the relevant technology has been tested and implemented on Eney, it plans to roll it out to more of its products, and hopes to open up the shared AI technology to Mac developers through Setapp.

This will allow participating apps to expose more features and contextual information to Eney, enabling the assistant to understand the internal state of the application and thereby provide more useful answers or perform relevant actions.

For more information about MacPaw's on-device AI technology and details of today's announcement, click here; you can also click here to learn about Liquid AI's latest developments.
